correctness.rationale: Every norm-five lattice vector has exactly one of two signed patterns (2,1,0...) or (1,1,1,1,1,0...), each an exposed vertex by equal norm and strict Cauchy–Schwarz. The signed-permutation support function is max{2s1+s2, s1+...+s5}. Polar sorted chamber in z_j=s_j-s_(j+1)>=0 has two positive linear constraints (2,3,3,...), (1,2,3,4,5,5,...); every vertex has at most two nonzero z, so convex squared norm max is at an enumerated vertex. Singles give 1/4,2/9,1/3,1/4,j/25; mixed (1,4)=7/25,(2,4)=5/18,(1,j>=5)=(j+8)/49,(2,j>=5)=(j+16)/81. The overall max is max{1/3,d/25,(d+8)/49,(d+16)/81}, switching uniquely from 1/3 through d=8 to d/25 at d>=9; thus r_d=sqrt3 then 5/sqrt(d). Sign-orbit unique maximizers give exact 8 C(d,3) or 2^d contact normals. Both representative support faces have rank d-1 (six 2/1 vectors plus complementary two ±1 coords, or all 5-ones vectors/hypersimplex). Contact normals span so incenter unique 0; antipodal shell gives unique center0 and R=sqrt5.
